# E3b — the contrast set: who writes the pragma, on loops DiscoPoP does not recognise as written

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

On six loops that DiscoPoP alone leaves unchanged and whose reference is one or a few directives away — chosen where a difference between the two setups is expected — does the agent ship more race-free verified faster programs where the model writes the pragma than where DiscoPoP writes it, and does anything wrong get through? One control loop DiscoPoP parallelizes itself. (RQ5; reported beside E3, not instead of it)

## Result in one paragraph

Read out 10 Oct (140 trials, 105 with model calls, no failed model call; every changed program of the agent race-clean). On the six loops under test the agent is race-free FASTER in 30 of 30 trials where the model writes the pragma and in 24 of 30 where DiscoPoP writes it — supported as a single test (exact one-sided p 0.0093, CMH 0.0135; three loops differ: `s315`, `s316`, `s318`), not established within the campaign's family (bound 0.49 from the exact p, 0.715 from the CMH p). Neither setup ships an unusable program in 35 trials; Haiku alone 27 of 30 with 3 unusable; DiscoPoP alone 0 of 30; the control 5 of 5 everywhere. What the count does not show: where DiscoPoP writes, the model mostly finds a form DiscoPoP recognises (`x = fmax(x, a[i])`, on which DiscoPoP itself writes `reduction(max:x)`, or an array filled in parallel and reduced afterwards) — with 179 model calls against 52, $29.59 against $6.03, and on four of the six loops less than half the speed (medians 3.32× against 8.73× on `s314`, 1.79× against 17.32× on `s318`). TO READ WITH IT: the premise the set was chosen on — that DiscoPoP has no pragma for a maximum — was wrong (it writes one on the `fmax` form; it does not recognise the loop as TSVC writes it; title corrected, the pre-registration in the record is not); a DiscoPoP defect found in these trials (B23: a minimum reported as a maximum, not repaired) fired in four of the five trials on `s316`, was refused by the gate each time, and can have cost at most one trial; the data hold no two equal largest values, so the position a program returns on a tie is not tested. Cost $38.11 (estimated $84). CORRECTED 11 Oct (`analysis/corrected/`): DiscoPoP B23 repaired on 10 Oct (the author: "Ok"; group B23) and `s316` run again in both setups and DiscoPoP alone on the repaired DiscoPoP (`e3bc_s316`, race check `e3bc_race_check`: every changed program clean) — where DiscoPoP writes, 4 of 5 (was 3), twice with DiscoPoP's own `reduction(min:x)` at the first model call, at 4.2 model calls a trial (was 9.2); where the model writes, 5 of 5 as before. The six loops: the model writes 30 of 30, DiscoPoP writes 25 of 30; exact one-sided p 0.0208 (CMH 0.0273) — supported as a single test, not within the family, as registered; no unusable program in either setup. The corrected table holds trials on two DiscoPoP versions (`s316` on the repaired one; on the other loops the repair changes nothing). $4.80.

No model has been called; none is called before the author has the exact cost.** **Why a pilot first** (the standing rule): step 2 asks whether the model's own account of the dependences of its rewrite gives DiscoPoP back what the fast refresh loses. Before that is paid for, it has to be seen that a CORRECT account does. **The pilot** (the Mac, 12 Oct, TSVC loops only; `results/E04_fast_refresh/analysis/report_pilot/`): for three of the 20 reductions of step 1 — a minimum (`s316`, repeat 1 of `e3b_1`, rewrite 1: `x = fmin(x, a[i]);`), a sum (`s319`, repeat 1 of `e3b_2`, rewrite 2: `sum += a[i] + b[i];`) and a maximum (`s3113`, repeat 2 of `e3b_2`, rewrite 1: `max = fmax(max, val);`) — the profile before the rewrite and the fast refresh are rebuilt with the replay tool, a report written by hand in the format the model is asked for (one line: `LOOP 9 RAW x 10 10`) goes through the agent's own `dep_reconstruct.reconstruct`, the explorer runs again and the rewrite is judged again as in step 1. **In all three** the line is placed as one row of the dependence file, DiscoPoP then writes the reduction on the model's loop — `reduction(min:x)`, `reduction(+:sum)`, `reduction(max:max)`, the directives of the full re-profile — the gate passes it, and the rewrite is kept. With the write-write dependence added as well the result is the same; a report that calls the loops independent changes nothing (the rewrite stays lost). After the fast refresh the reduction file already holds the entry for the model's loop in all three (the compile writes it): only the dependence was missing. On `s316` and `s3113` DiscoPoP still offers a directive on the repetition loop as well, which the race detector refuses as before; on `s319` the verdict is exactly the full profile's. **What this shows and what it does not:** the path from a correct report to the kept reduction works on the three operators; whether the model writes that report, and what its reports do to the rewrites whose decision the fast refresh did not change, is step 2's question. **The opposite direction on the three** (the model deletes dependences it calls unreal): the agent's review asks only about Do-All blockers that come from static analysis and lie in the rewritten lines; on the three there is none (no blocker recorded in two, one of measured origin in the third), so nothing would be asked. The fast refresh leaves these loops unblocked, not over-blocked.
